raw.overview: Start your Paris adventure in the vibrant Marais, savoring tasty bites and diving into poignant history, all at a relaxed walking pace.

days.summary: A balanced day of delicious food stops and moving historical sites.

stops.description: Grab a quick, tasty lunch at Les Enfants Rouges, the city’s oldest covered market, where you can sample fresh, affordable bites from diverse stalls—perfect for a solo foodie on a budget.
stops.tip: Arrive early to avoid the lunch rush and try the falafel or a fresh tartine.

stops.description: Visit Charlotte Delbo, a solemn memorial honoring the French Resistance heroine, offering a reflective glimpse into WWII history that resonates with solo travelers seeking depth.
stops.tip: Allow extra time for the audio guide; it enriches the experience.

stops.description: Enjoy a relaxed French bistro lunch at Bistro des Poèmes, where classic dishes are served in a literary‑themed setting, giving you a taste of Parisian culture and cuisine.
stops.tip: Ask for the daily special—it’s often the best value and changes frequently.

stops.description: Explore Jacob Kaplan, a moving memorial that tells the story of a lesser‑known resistance figure, blending personal narratives with broader historical context.
stops.tip: Bring a notebook to jot down names and dates; the plaques are dense with information.

stops.description: Wander through Thermes de Cluny, the archaeological site of ancient Roman baths, where you can imagine daily life in antiquity while enjoying the open‑air stone arches.
stops.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; the stone floors can be uneven.

stops.description: End the day at La Robe et le Palais, a cozy bistro offering classic French fare in a relaxed atmosphere, ideal for a solo dinner after a day of walking and learning.
stops.tip: Reserve a table for the evening to guarantee a seat, especially on weekends.

stops.name: Les Enfants Rouges
stops.description: Start your day with a relaxed breakfast‑lunch at Paris’ oldest covered market. Grab a fresh croissant, a savory tartine or a tasty falafel from one of the stalls – perfect fuel for a day of walking and a great way to taste the multicultural bite of the Marais.
stops.tip: Arrive early to beat the crowd and ask for the “menu du jour” – it’s usually the best value.

stops.name: Charlotte Delbo
stops.description: A short walk brings you to the Charlotte Delbo memorial plaque, honoring the French Resistance heroine. Take a moment to read the text and reflect on the city’s wartime bravery – a poignant slice of history for a first‑time visitor.
stops.tip: Bring a notebook; the plaque is small but the story is big, and you’ll want to remember it.

stops.name: Bistro des Poèmes
stops.description: Nestled in the literary‑rich 6th arrondissement, this cozy bistro serves classic French dishes at reasonable prices. Enjoy a leisurely lunch of quiche Lorraine or a seasonal salad while soaking up the neighborhood’s historic charm.
stops.tip: Ask for the “plat du jour” and a glass of house wine – it’s the best way to stay on budget without sacrificing taste.

stops.name: Jacob Kaplan
stops.description: Continue your historical thread with the Jacob Kaplan memorial plaque, a quiet reminder of the Jewish community’s legacy in Paris. The site sits on a pleasant pedestrian street, perfect for a reflective stroll.
stops.tip: Combine this stop with a quick coffee at a nearby café; the area has several charming spots with outdoor seating.

stops.name: Thermes de Cluny
stops.description: Dive into ancient Roman‑by‑medieval layers at the Thermes de Cluny, an archaeological site beneath the Musée de Cluny. Explore the well‑preserved baths and imagine daily life in Gallo‑Roman Paris – a perfect blend of history and intrigue for a solo explorer.
stops.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; the underground passages can be a bit uneven, and the site closes early in winter.

stops.name: La Robe et le Palais
stops.description: End the day with a relaxed dinner at this elegant bistro, offering a refined yet affordable French menu. The ambience, with both indoor and outdoor seating, lets you unwind after a day of walking while still staying within a mixed budget.
stops.tip: Reserve a table for the terrace if the weather is nice – it’s a lovely spot to watch Parisians wind down.

days.summary: From market bites to hidden memorials and ancient baths, the day weaves food and history into a balanced Parisian adventure.

raw.overview: You’ll wander from the bustling Les Enfants Rouges market through quiet historic plaques, savor a classic bistro lunch, explore Roman‑era baths, and finish with a delightful dinner—all on foot, at a comfortable pace, and with a mix of free and reasonably priced experiences.

trip.notes: I love street food and want great photo spots.

stops.name: Charlotte Delbo

stops.tip: Take a moment to read the inscription in French; a quick translation app will help you catch the details.

stops.name: Bistro des Poèmes
stops.description: Lunch at this literary‑themed bistro offers classic French dishes in a cozy setting – ideal for a balanced pace and a chance to refuel before more walking. The décor provides great photo opportunities for your Instagram feed.
stops.tip: Ask for the daily prix‑fixe menu; it’s the best value and often includes a glass of house wine.

stops.name: Jacob Kaplan
stops.description: After lunch, wander to the Jacob Kaplan memorial. This modest plaque tells the story of a lesser‑known figure of the Holocaust, adding depth to your historical tour and giving you a quiet moment to reflect.

stops.name: Thermes de Cluny

stops.name: La Robe et le Palais

days.summary: A tasty, history‑rich walk from market stalls to ancient baths, ending with a sunset dinner.

raw.overview: You’ll wander from the lively Les Enfants Rouges market, dip into poignant memorials, savor a literary bistro lunch, discover Roman baths, and wrap up with a charming dinner on a terrace – all at a comfortable pace and full of photo‑worthy moments.

raw.overview: Start your Tokyo adventure in Shinjuku and wander through a curated mix of tasty eats and lively bars, all at a relaxed pace perfect for a solo first‑timer.

days.summary: From a hearty lunch to buzzing bars, experience Tokyo’s food and nightlife on foot.

stops.description: Enjoy a quick, satisfying meal at 華屋, where you can sample classic Japanese comfort food perfect for fueling your day.
stops.tip: Bring cash; many small eateries don’t take cards.

stops.description: Stop at 番番 for another tasty bite, offering a cozy atmosphere ideal for a solo traveler to relax before the evening.
stops.tip: Check the menu board outside for prices and specials.

stops.description: Head to CHAMPION, a lively bar where you can sip cocktails and soak up the energetic nightlife scene.
stops.tip: Arrive early to snag a good spot; the bar gets crowded after 8 PM.

stops.description: Ale offers a relaxed pub vibe with a good selection of drinks, perfect for winding down after CHAMPION while still staying in the action.
stops.tip: Try the house draft; it’s often a local favorite.

stops.description: 創作DINING彩 blends creative drinks with a modern setting, giving you a taste of Tokyo’s innovative bar culture.
stops.tip: Ask the staff for the seasonal recommendation—they love showcasing new flavors.

stops.description: End the day at 友人, an Indian restaurant where you can enjoy aromatic dishes and a comforting finish to your Tokyo tour.
stops.tip: Many Indian spots serve lunch sets; ask for the vegetarian option if you prefer.

stops.name: 華屋
stops.description: Start your day with a hearty Japanese breakfast at 華屋, a local eatery near Shinjuku. The menu offers classic set meals that give you a solid energy boost for the walk ahead, perfect for a solo first‑timer who loves food.
stops.tip: Pay cash and ask for a take‑away box if you want to enjoy the meal on a park bench later.

stops.name: 番番
stops.description: Walk to 番番, a tucked‑away noodle shop where you can choose between soba or udon from a vending‑machine ticket. It’s cheap, quick, and gives you a taste of everyday Tokyo street food – exactly what a budget‑conscious solo traveler craves.
stops.tip: Look for the picture menu on the machine; you can point to the dish even if you don’t read Japanese.

stops.name: CHAMPION
stops.description: Mid‑day, head to CHAMPION, a lively bar in Shinjuku that doubles as a casual lunch spot. The upbeat vibe and easy‑going crowd make it a great place to mingle or simply enjoy a drink while people‑watching, fitting your nightlife curiosity.
stops.tip: Try the house‑made cocktail and ask for a nomihōdai (all‑you‑can‑drink) option if you’re feeling adventurous.

stops.name: Ale
stops.description: After a short walk, stop at Ale, a rooftop‑style bar with a relaxed atmosphere. It’s perfect for a balanced‑pace traveler who wants a sip of craft beer without the rush of a crowded izakaya.
stops.tip: Check the happy‑hour board; many places offer discounted drafts before 6 PM.

stops.name: 創作DINING彩
stops.description: Continue the evening at 創作DINING彩, a stylish pub that blends creative small plates with a vibrant bar scene. It satisfies your love of food and nightlife in one stop, letting you sample inventive Japanese‑fusion bites.
stops.tip: Reserve a seat at the bar counter so you can watch the chefs plate the dishes – it’s a fun visual treat.

stops.name: 友人
stops.description: Wrap up the day with dinner at 友人, an Indian‑style restaurant offering aromatic curries and naan. It’s a comforting end to a food‑focused day and gives you a chance to unwind after a full evening of exploring Tokyo’s bar scene.
stops.tip: Ask for the mild “butter chicken” if you’re not used to spicy food; most places will adjust the heat level.

days.summary: From a morning Japanese set meal to evening Indian flavors, the day blends tasty stops with relaxed bar hops, all on foot.

raw.overview: I’ve mapped a tasty, balanced walk from Shinjuku that lets you sample local breakfasts, quick noodle bites, and three distinct nightlife spots before ending with a comforting Indian dinner – perfect for a solo first‑timer who loves food and a lively evening.

trip.notes: No bars or pubs please, I don't drink.

raw.overview: Start your Tokyo adventure in Shinjuku with a tasty breakfast, wander through a bustling street food haven, and finish with a comforting Indian dinner. The day balances delicious eats with a relaxed pace, letting you soak up the city’s energy without any drinking venues.

days.summary: A culinary walk from sunrise to sunset, perfect for a solo first‑timer.

stops.description: Kick off with a hearty Japanese breakfast at 華屋, where you can try classic dishes like tamagoyaki and miso soup – a warm welcome for a solo traveler.
stops.tip: Arrive a few minutes early to pick a seat; the place fills up quickly during morning rush.

stops.description: Next, head to 番番 for a quick lunch of sushi or tempura; the menu is displayed outside, making it easy to choose and pay with cash.
stops.tip: Bring ¥500–¥800 in cash; many small eateries don’t accept cards.

stops.description: CHAMPION is listed as a nightlife spot, but since you prefer no bars, you might simply admire the lively atmosphere from the street and skip entering.
stops.tip: If you change your mind, check the opening hours; some venues have early‑evening food service.

stops.description: Ale is another bar‑type stop; you can use the brief walk to explore nearby side streets and maybe pop into a convenience store for a snack.
stops.tip: Look for a Lawson 100 nearby for affordable onigiri and drinks.

stops.description: 創作DINING彩 is a pub‑style venue; consider passing by to enjoy the exterior lights and then continue toward your dinner destination.
stops.tip: Take a quick photo of the neon signage for a souvenir.

stops.description: End the day at 友人, an Indian restaurant where you can savor flavorful curries and naan – a satisfying, non‑alcoholic dinner after a full day of walking.
stops.tip: Reserve a seat if possible; evenings can get busy, especially on weekends.

stops.name: 華屋
stops.description: Start your day with a hearty Japanese breakfast at 華屋. This local eatery serves classic dishes like tamagoyaki and grilled fish – perfect fuel for a day of walking and food‑loving adventures.
stops.tip: Arrive early; the place fills up quickly at breakfast time.

stops.name: 番番
stops.description: Next, head to 番番 for a quick lunch of udon or soba from the vending‑machine ticket system. The casual counter setting lets you watch the chefs work, a fun glimpse into everyday Tokyo dining.
stops.tip: Grab a seat at the counter for the fastest service and a chance to ask the staff for recommendations in English.

stops.name: 友人
stops.description: Wrap up with dinner at 友人, an Indian‑style restaurant offering flavorful curries and naan. It’s a nice change of pace after a day of Japanese fare and fits your love of diverse food without any alcohol focus.
stops.tip: Ask for a mild curry if you’re new to Indian spice; the staff are happy to adjust the heat level.

days.summary: A relaxed food‑focused stroll through Shinjuku’s neighborhoods, sampling both Japanese classics and international flavors.

raw.overview: You’ll wander from a traditional breakfast spot to a bustling noodle shop, then end the evening with a tasty Indian dinner – all on foot, with plenty of time to soak up the local vibe and keep your budget friendly.

raw.overview: Start your Roman adventure in Trastevere and wander through a curated mix of historic memorials and museums, balancing indoor depth with brief outdoor moments, all at a relaxed pace for a solo first‑timer.

days.summary: A day of statues, museums, and ancient ruins that brings Rome’s layered history to life.

stops.description: Admire the striking statue at Gregorio Nazianzeno, a perfect snapshot of Rome’s historic artistry that sets the tone for your day.
stops.tip: Arrive a few minutes early to avoid the brief crowd that gathers for photos.

stops.description: Explore the Real Academia de España, where cultural exhibitions showcase Spain’s influence on Italian art, offering a quiet indoor retreat.
stops.tip: Check the exhibition guide at the entrance to focus on pieces that match your interests.

stops.description: Dive into the Museo di Roma’s collections, a vivid narrative of the city’s evolution from ancient times to modern life.
stops.tip: Grab the free audio guide; it’s concise and fits the 90‑minute slot.

stops.description: Visit the Museo Universale for a curated look at universal art themes, complementing your earlier historic stops with broader cultural context.
stops.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; the museum’s layout involves several short staircases.

stops.description: Stand before the Testa di Costantino, a striking marble bust that connects you directly to the emperor’s legacy in the heart of the city.
stops.tip: Take a moment to read the nearby plaque; it offers quick historical insight without needing a guide.

stops.description: End your day at the Domus Augustana – Peristilio, wandering the ancient Roman palace ruins and feeling the grandeur of imperial life.
stops.tip: Bring a small bottle of water and a light jacket; the open courtyard can be cool even in mild weather.

stops.name: Gregorio Nazianzeno
stops.description: Start your morning with a quiet pause at this modest memorial statue. The artwork, set in a leafy square, lets you feel Rome’s layered history without the crowds – perfect for a solo traveler who loves history at a relaxed pace.
stops.tip: Arrive early to avoid the occasional street market; the stone bench nearby is great for a quick coffee.

stops.name: Real Academia de España
stops.description: Cross the Tiber to the tranquil Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio and explore this little‑known museum of Spanish art and cultural ties. It satisfies your cultural curiosity while staying free of the tourist throngs.
stops.tip: Check the free‑entry hours on the plaque; the museum often offers a short guided talk in English on weekends.

stops.name: Museo di Roma
stops.description: Wander through Palazzo Braschi’s rooms to see Rome’s evolution from medieval streets to modern boulevards. The mix of artifacts and vivid frescoes matches your love for both history and culture.
stops.tip: Buy a combined ticket for the museum and the nearby Villa Doria Pamphili garden to stretch your lunch break.

stops.name: Museo Universale
stops.description: A short walk brings you to this eclectic museum where science, art and archaeology intersect. It offers a balanced, hands‑on experience that keeps the day lively without rushing.
stops.tip: Bring a reusable water bottle; there’s a refill station near the entrance.

stops.name: Testa di Costantino
stops.description: Pause beside the colossal head of Constantine, a striking reminder of imperial power. The open square lets you soak up the late‑afternoon light and reflect on Rome’s imperial past.
stops.tip: Watch for street musicians – they often play near the monument and add a lively soundtrack to your visit.

stops.name: Domus Augustana - Peristilio
stops.description: End the day exploring the ruins of Augustus’ grand palace. The peristyle’s columns and quiet courtyards feel like stepping back into ancient Rome, fitting your balanced pace and love of history.
stops.tip: Stay until closing to experience the golden hour light filtering through the arches – it’s magical for photos.

days.summary: A day of quiet monuments, hidden museums, and ancient ruins that lets you breathe Rome’s history at a comfortable walk.

raw.overview: From Trastevere you’ll stroll through lesser‑known squares, pop into a handful of intimate museums, and finish among the ruins of Augustus’ palace – a perfect mix of free and paid sights for a solo history lover.

trip.notes: I've already seen the main museum, skip museums.

stops.tip: Buy a timed ticket online to skip any queue.

stops.description: Wander through the Museo Universale, a compact venue that blends contemporary installations with historic references, giving you a fresh perspective on Rome’s artistic dialogue.
stops.tip: Look for the free audio guide on your phone for concise explanations.

stops.description: Stand before the Testa di Costantino, the preserved marble head of the emperor, and imagine the grandeur of the ancient capital.

days.theme: Historic walk from Trastevere to the heart of ancient Rome

stops.name: Gregorio Nazianzeno
stops.description: Start your day with a quiet moment at this historic memorial statue. The artwork by Giovanni Maria de Rossi offers a glimpse into Rome’s layered past, perfect for a history‑lover who enjoys off‑the‑beaten‑path gems.
stops.tip: Arrive early to avoid the late‑morning crowd and snap photos with the soft morning light.

stops.name: Real Academia de España
stops.description: Cross the Tiber and wander into Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio to see the elegant façade of the Spanish Academy. Though listed as a museum, entry is free, letting you soak up cultural ambience without spending a euro.
stops.tip: Check the door for any temporary closures; the building is often open to the public for brief tours.

stops.name: Museo di Roma
stops.description: A short walk brings you to this museum housed in Palazzo Braschi. It tells the story of Rome from its medieval streets to modern life—great for a first‑time visitor craving context without another big museum experience.
stops.tip: Buy a combined ticket for the museum and the nearby Capitoline Museums if you decide to extend your cultural dive later.

stops.name: Museo Universale
stops.description: Continue east to this quirky venue that showcases universal themes—art, science, and history—in a compact space. It balances free‑entry curiosity with a modest fee, fitting your mixed‑budget vibe.
stops.tip: Bring a small amount of cash; the ticket office sometimes prefers it over cards.

stops.name: Testa di Costantino
stops.description: Walk to the iconic Colossus of Constantine’s head, a striking reminder of imperial power. The open‑air setting lets you enjoy the Roman light while contemplating ancient history.
stops.tip: Look up to see the remaining fragments of the statue’s crown for a dramatic photo.

stops.name: Domus Augustana - Peristilio
stops.description: End your day amid the ruins of the Emperor’s palace. The peristyle courtyard offers a serene, slightly secluded spot to reflect on the day’s discoveries, ideal for a balanced‑pace solo explorer.
stops.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; the ancient stone can be uneven, especially in the late afternoon light.

days.summary: A leisurely trek through Rome’s hidden historic corners, blending free sights and modestly priced culture.

raw.overview: From Trastevere you’ll wander eastward, stopping at statues, quiet academies, and ancient ruins, all at a relaxed pace that lets you soak in Rome’s layered past without museum fatigue.
Start your London adventure in vibrant Soho, then wander through tasty brunch spots, lively pubs and a relaxed dinner, all at a comfortable pace for a solo first‑timer who loves food and nightlife.

days.summary: A balanced six‑hour stroll mixing delicious bites with buzzing pubs, ending with craft beer on the South Bank.

stops.description: Grab a hearty breakfast at The Chancery, a cosy spot perfect for fueling up before a day of walking and tasting London flavours.
stops.tip: Arrive early to avoid the morning rush and ask for the house toast with jam.

stops.description: Enjoy a relaxed brunch at City Brunch, where the café vibe and solid coffee give you a gentle transition to the city’s buzz.
stops.tip: Try the avocado toast and ask for a refill on the coffee – it’s free.

stops.description: Head to The Victory for an early afternoon pint; this pub’s lively atmosphere and classic British ales match your nightlife interest while still being daytime friendly.
stops.tip: Sit at the bar for faster service and chat with the bartender about local brews.

stops.description: Continue the pub crawl at Bbar, a stylish venue where you can sip cocktails or craft beers in a relaxed setting before dinner.
stops.tip: Check the cocktail menu for a house special and ask for a low‑alcohol version if you plan to keep going.

stops.description: Dine at The Shell, a restaurant open late with a menu that blends British comfort food and modern twists, ideal for a solo dinner after a day of exploring.
stops.tip: Reserve a small table online to guarantee a seat, and ask for the chef’s tasting sampler.

stops.description: End the night at Craft Beer Co., a bustling pub with an extensive tap list, perfect for winding down and meeting locals after a full day of food and fun.
stops.tip: Ask the staff for the ‘flight of the day’ to sample several brews without over‑indulging.

days.theme: Taste of London, day to night

stops.name: The Chancery
stops.description: Start your London adventure with a hearty English breakfast or brunch at The Chancery. The venue’s classic British vibe gives a solo traveler a relaxed setting to fuel up before a day of exploring, and the menu balances affordable comfort food with a few upscale options – perfect for a mixed budget.
stops.tip: Arrive early to snag a window seat and ask for the "liquor" gravy if you want to try authentic pie‑and‑mash style gravy.

stops.name: City Brunch
stops.description: Walk east to City Brunch for a lighter mid‑morning bite. This café’s outdoor seating lets you soak up the street buzz while enjoying fresh pastries or a savory sandwich – ideal for a solo traveler who likes to keep the pace balanced and stay energized.
stops.tip: Check the chalkboard for any seasonal specials; they often feature locally sourced ingredients at a great price.

stops.name: The Victory
stops.description: After lunch, head north to The Victory, a historic pub with a lively atmosphere. It offers a solid selection of ales and a relaxed vibe that’s popular with locals, giving you a genuine nightlife taste without the tourist‑trap prices.
stops.tip: Try the house pint and ask the bartender for a recommendation on a local craft brew; they’ll often have a hidden gem on tap.

stops.name: Bbar
stops.description: Mid‑afternoon, wander to Bbar near Buckingham Palace Road. This sleek venue blends a cocktail bar feel with a small plates menu, perfect for a solo traveler looking to sip something inventive while people‑watch in a stylish setting.
stops.tip: Order the signature gin‑infused cocktail and ask for a small tasting platter to keep costs balanced.

stops.name: The Shell
stops.description: As evening approaches, stroll to The Shell for a relaxed dinner. The restaurant’s late‑opening hours and varied menu let you enjoy a sit‑down meal after a few drinks, rounding off the day with comfort food that still feels a step up from fast‑food fare.
stops.tip: Reserve a table for one via their website to avoid the rush and request a seat near the window for a view of the bustling street.

stops.name: Craft Beer Co.
stops.description: End the night in Covent Garden’s Craft Beer Co., a lively spot with real ales, craft kegs, and a buzzing crowd. It’s the perfect finale for a nightlife‑loving solo traveler, offering a mix of affordable pints and a vibrant social scene.
stops.tip: Bring a reusable bottle for the tap‑water refill station and ask the staff which seasonal brew is on tap tonight.

stops.name: The Shell

days.summary: A balanced day of food, theatre and local atmosphere, all within easy walking distance.

stops.description: Grab a fresh, organic breakfast at a nearby café, perfect for fueling your day with healthy local flavors.
stops.tip: Arrive a few minutes early to choose a seat on the patio and enjoy the morning light.

stops.description: Catch a short performance or tour at the historic Condal theatre, immersing you in Barcelona’s rich performing‑arts heritage.
stops.tip: Check the programme online and book a free or low‑cost matinee if available.

stops.description: Visit the intimate Cafè‑Teatre el Llantiol for a blend of live music and cultural events, offering a genuine local experience.
stops.tip: Bring a small cash tip for the performers; many venues rely on audience generosity.

stops.description: Enjoy a quick, tasty pizza lunch at Italo, a casual spot that lets you refuel without slowing down your itinerary.
stops.tip: Order the house special and ask for a take‑away box if you want to snack while strolling.

stops.description: Step into the elegant Teatre Romea for another dose of Barcelona’s theatrical tradition, ideal for a solo traveler who loves culture.
stops.tip: Dress smart‑casual; the venue has a modest dress code for evening shows.

stops.description: End the day with a relaxed dinner at Sagarra, a restaurant serving classic Catalan dishes in a welcoming setting.

stops.name: Organic
stops.description: Start your day with a relaxed breakfast at Organic, a cozy spot serving fresh, locally‑sourced dishes. The menu leans toward healthy Catalan fare, perfect for a solo traveler who wants to fuel up before a day of walking and culture.
stops.tip: Arrive early; the place fills up quickly and they offer a complimentary coffee if you order a pastry before 10 am.

stops.name: Condal
stops.description: Walk to the historic Teatre Condal, an elegant early‑20th‑century theatre that still hosts plays and concerts. Its beautiful façade and interior give you a taste of Barcelona’s cultural heritage without the crowds of larger venues.
stops.tip: Check the schedule at the ticket desk; many shows have a reduced “cultura” price for locals and solo visitors.

stops.name: Cafè-Teatre el Llantiol
stops.description: Stroll to this intimate café‑theatre on Carrer de la Riereta. Enjoy a quick coffee while catching a short stand‑up comedy or a local music set—great for soaking up the creative vibe of the Gothic Quarter’s side streets.
stops.tip: Ask for the “menú del día” at the bar; it includes a small tapa and a drink for under €10.

stops.name: Italo
stops.description: For lunch, head to Italo, a fast‑food pizza joint loved by locals for its thin‑crust slices and quick service. It’s a budget‑friendly way to keep the momentum going while still tasting a bit of Mediterranean flair.
stops.tip: Order the “pizza de la casa” and pair it with a small glass of house wine for a true Catalan twist.

stops.name: Teatre Romea
stops.description: After lunch, wander to Teatre Romea, a classic venue on Carrer de l'Hospital. Its ornate interior and regular schedule of theatre, dance, and jazz makes it a cultural highlight that matches your love of arts and balanced pacing.
stops.tip: Buy a standing‑room ticket at the box office for the best price; the acoustics are excellent even from the back.

stops.name: Sagarra
stops.description: End the afternoon with a light dinner at Sagarra, a modest restaurant offering traditional Catalan dishes like pa amb tomàquet and grilled fish. It’s a relaxed spot where you can reflect on the day’s discoveries.
stops.tip: Ask for the “menu del día” – it includes a starter, main, dessert, and a glass of house wine for a very reasonable price.

days.summary: A day of tasty bites and intimate cultural venues, all within easy walking distance from the Gothic Quarter.

raw.overview: You’ll wander from a fresh‑food breakfast through historic theatres and a quick pizza lunch, finishing with a classic Catalan dinner—perfect for a solo traveler who loves culture and food without rushing.
